section.settings: Researcher's settings (these take precedence over example values in this document)
section.papers: Source papers (in the project's citation scope)

settings.askBeforeStep: Ask the researcher about a condition that is not set before the step that uses it.
settings.runThrough: Every condition is set. Record details the settings and instructions leave open as assumptions (the recommended or source value) and run to the end. Stop and ask only when a required input is missing or its format or CRS does not fit.
settings.cliArguments: The values after the command are the researcher's settings:
settings.cliAsk: Before you start, ask the researcher for any item below that those values do not give.
settings.researcherPicksExample: chosen by the researcher. If none is chosen, the Workflow's example data is used: {title}
settings.examplesUsed: These inputs are not the researcher's data but example data supplied with the Workflow: {labels}
settings.exampleRule: When running on example data, state at the top of the answer, the result files and the research note that example data was used. Do not present results for the example area as conclusions about the researcher's study area.
settings.cliExample: If no value is given, use the Workflow's example data: {title} (source: {source}). Files: {files}
settings.cliExampleRemote: {url} (after downloading, check size {size} bytes and sha256 {sha256})

skill.readRule: Before you start a step that uses a skill, read that skill's instruction file (SKILL.md).

steps.legacy: This Workflow uses the earlier format. For the detailed method of each step, follow the procedure in the instructions of skill {skill}.

closing.review: The results are not reviewed yet. Do not report a completed run as a completed review.
closing.examples: If example values in this document (target, resolution, data size and so on) differ from the researcher's settings or the actual files, follow the settings and the files and say what differs first.

card.label: Workflow · {title}
card.pendingHint: When you send, these Workflow instructions go first and what you type follows them.
card.fallback: {count, plural, one {# input without data} other {# inputs without data}}

papers.rule: The papers the Workflow is based on. Check them with library_search and library_read, and cite them as [@key] in the research note where a method or threshold comes from them.

fallback.intro: The researcher has no data for the inputs below. Before the first step, provide data for each input as chosen. Ask everything needed together with the interview tool, and do not download or generate data before the answer.

value.search: no data; the AI agent finds similar public data
value.synthetic: no data; the AI agent generates synthetic data
value.instruction: no data; follow the researcher's separate instruction

rule.search: Find similar public data: use web search to find a small public dataset of the same format and kind as the input. Show 2-3 candidates with source URL, provider, terms of use, size, area and format, and download only the candidate the researcher picks.
rule.searchLimit: Do not download data whose terms are unclear, that needs a login or that is larger than 100 MB; say why it was not downloaded. If no candidate fits, ask whether to use synthetic data.
rule.searchRecord: Next to the downloaded files, write SOURCE.md with the source URL, download date, terms of use and each file's sha256.
rule.synthetic: Generate synthetic data: before generating, confirm with the researcher what the data must represent (subject and scale, value ranges and units, CRS, noise or gaps). Keep the generating code (fixed random seed) and a README.md stating the assumptions in the same folder.
rule.instruction: Separate instruction: follow the researcher's instruction. Ask first when it is ambiguous, or when data must be downloaded or generated and the instruction does not say how.
rule.label: For results from such data, state at the top and in the limits of the answer, the result files and the research note that similar public data (toy data) or synthetic data was used. Do not present the results as conclusions about the researcher's study area or real data.

digest.rule: Before analysis, read the digest first with library_digest. Verify every claim used in results with library_read on the original paper pages and cite [@key, p. N]. Never cite the digest itself.
digest.externalRule: An external summary (Gemini Notebook) is reference only. A confirmed mark does not replace checking the original papers.
